BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Overall assessment:** The Seller package is not "fair and balanced" from our side. It (a) opens at our *unauthorised* fallback levels on cap and time limit, (b) collapses Fundamental/Title, Tax and IP into the general regime, (c) deploys whole-data-room disclosure plus a blanket buyer-knowledge bar, and (d) leaves Bluefen, Riverlark and the DD-005 bonuses unresolved despite the Disclosure Letter itself conceding they are unresolved. No Amelia Frost written authority exists for any fallback, so we hold playbook starting positions throughout.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Cl 12.1 – 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.**
  *Reason:* 20% is our conditional fallback only and no Amelia Frost written authority identifying this draft has been given – we cannot concede it as an opening response.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** Cl 12.2 – de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery.
- **Buyer wants:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject all three elements; counter at playbook levels with tipping basket.**
  *Reason:* Seller's thresholds are 5× ours and the deductible structure permanently forfeits the first AUD 250,000 of loss – a double concession not in our mandate.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** Cl 12.3/13 – 18 months; plus "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months; limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims as expressly drafted.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.**
  *Reason:* 18 months is an unapproved fallback, and the default-application sentence is a back-door override of the Fundamental/Tax/IP/indemnity regimes (see N-014).

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum 6 years, outside general basket, de minimis and any knowledge qualifier.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright; insert standalone Fundamental Warranty regime.**
  *Reason:* Capping title at 20% means a total title failure recovers AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m purchase – "administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept that.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"; no fraud carve-out appears anywhere.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Non-negotiable; insert express carve-out and reject "all Claims of any nature."**
  *Reason:* This is a playbook item no one on the deal team may waive, and the Seller's drafting would purport to limit liability for its own fraud.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Sch 7 / DL [1.1]–[1.2] – general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records; [1.4] reserves all admissions.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject [1.1]–[1.2]; require "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope" standard and a specific disclosure schedule against each warranty.**
  *Reason:* Whole-data-room disclosure would qualify every warranty by everything we were shown, gutting the warranty package.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Cl 8.3 – no claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Buyer wants:** Delete. If any qualifier survives, limit it to actual knowledge of named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never applicable to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3 in full.**
  *Reason:* "Discoverable" imputed knowledge combined with N-006 means every disclosed-or-findable issue is doubly excluded – it is a constructive-knowledge bar dressed as a knowledge qualifier.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Cl 3/6.3 – reasonable endeavours; condition "satisfied on delivery" of counterparty's written consent. DL §2 admits no final consent and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** Condition precedent requiring effective consent under cl 11.2 **and** evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; not satisfied merely on delivery.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; redraft as a hard CP with evidence of condition satisfaction, Buyer reasonable-satisfaction standard, and no "reasonable endeavours"-only obligation.**
  *Reason:* Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m); a conditional consent whose conditions are unmet is not a consent.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Cl 2/7 – ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion." DL §3 confirms not repaid, no discharge in data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds on the funds flow, and effective security releases/discharges delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject post-completion release; require payout figure, direct pay-off and executed releases as Completion deliverables.** Any post-completion release needs an irrevocable bank undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval (none given).
  *Reason:* Debt-free/cash-free pricing cannot sit alongside AUD 3.2m of secured debt surviving Completion on a promise to release later.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** Funds flow – DD-005 AUD 420,000 bonuses "a matter for the Seller," not itemised. DL §5 confirms omission and is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs either a specific funds-flow line item (deducted/paid by Seller) or expressly Seller-funded with indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Require specific line item or Seller-funded treatment with on-costs; request Seller confirm the on-cost position.**
  *Reason:* A "matter for the Seller" that is not in the funds flow becomes a Company (i.e. Buyer) liability the moment Completion triggers it.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Cl 11.1 – indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "adequate." DL §4: cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of all fees; AUD 180,000 shown open in DD-010 but not independently verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:** Broader indemnity covering failure of IP transfer, defect in title to Project Materials and consequential loss, while preserving the SOW3 cure (pay-to-transfer) route; a pre-Completion deliverable of payment evidence and confirmatory assignment.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "adequate"; broaden the indemnity and add confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable.** Treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified in either direction – do not price it, and do not accept Seller's framing that it is the whole exposure.
  *Reason:* The exposure is loss of IP ownership, not a fixed invoice; an indemnity capped at the invoice misses the real risk.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** Cl 4.6/Sch 6 – "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material. DL §6: ~1,240 records; access, scope and notification duty all undetermined; no loss figure.
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, completed investigation, ongoing update covenant, and a specific indemnity for notification/remediation costs and regulatory exposure arising from DD-006; no materiality characterisation either way.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "not material"; require preservation/investigation/update covenants and a specific indemnity.** Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantum – do not let either side numeric it yet.
  *Reason:* "Preliminary" means unknown, and unknown privacy exposure on a share purchase passes to us at Completion unless ring-fenced.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000 "ordinary-course operating costs." DL §8 is silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course; DD-008/DD-011 to be read together.
- **Buyer wants:** Assessment of timing, terminability and accrual status; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** **Accept neither characterisation; issue a targeted DD request (terms, termination rights, accrual, renewal dates) before Completion Accounts treatment is agreed.**
  *Reason:* Seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported by its own disclosure, but we have no basis yet to treat the amounts as Debt either.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Cl 12.3/13 default ("applies to all Claims"), cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 ("all Claims of any nature"), Fundamental folded in, Tax/IP "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment/leakage and covenant claims each in their own regime; no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject every override mechanism; insert an express precedence clause that general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and do not apply to Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnity, leakage or covenant claims.**
  *Reason:* Four separate drafting devices are doing the same job – collapsing everything into the 20%/18-month box – and each must be removed for the separate regimes to mean anything.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title to 100% evidenced by the DD-012 share register. DL §10 concedes this is the source relied on and does not state Buyer has verified.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence – ASIC extract, share certificates, PPSR and charge searches, constitution review, board/shareholder authority evidence, and confirmation of no encumbrances or pre-emption rights.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept DD-012 as proof; commission independent title/encumbrance/authority verification and add corresponding Completion deliverables.**
  *Reason:* A company-maintained register supplied by the Seller is the thing being verified, not the verification.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP remain OPEN, negotiated as separate regimes (own cap and period); assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled"; record Tax and IP as open items in the issues list and respond with separate proposed regimes.**
  *Reason:* Nothing has been agreed – the Seller is characterising silence as settlement to lock Tax/IP into the 20%/18-month cap.

---

## Priority order for the mark-up
1. **Structural (must fix first):** N-005 fraud carve-out, N-014 category separation, N-004 Fundamental regime, N-016 Tax/IP open.
2. **Completion mechanics:** N-008 Bluefen CP, N-009 Riverlark payoff, N-010 bonuses in funds flow, N-015 title verification.
3. **Economics:** N-001 cap, N-002 thresholds, N-003 time limit.
4. **Specific risk allocation:** N-011 Ironquay, N-012 DD-006 incident, N-013 Sandbar.
5. **Disclosure architecture:** N-006 and N-007 (should be run together – they compound).

**Authority note:** No fallback positions (20% cap, 18-month period, post-completion Riverlark release) may be offered until Amelia Frost gives written approval identifying this draft. None is on file.
